meta.teaser: Build, test and publish your own obstacle course in Roblox Studio.

page.title: Make your first Roblox obby: from player to creator
page.sub: A skill you can use today
page.bigIdea: Alex Balfanz started making Roblox games at age 9. Later he co-created Jailbreak, with nearly 8 billion visits. Every creator starts with one simple build.

cards.title: Start with the template
cards.front: Roblox Studio has a free Classic Obby template to learn from.
cards.back: It starts easy and gets harder. It has moving platforms, launch pads and blocks that reset your health.
cards.tryit: Open the Classic Obby template, click Play and finish it. Which obstacle was hardest?

cards.title: Add platforms with parts
cards.front: Every platform in an obby is a part.
cards.back: Use the Part inserter on the Home tab. Pick a shape: Block, Sphere, Cylinder, Wedge or Corner Wedge.
cards.tryit: Add 5 new platforms using at least 3 different shapes.

cards.title: Move, scale, rotate
cards.front: The gap between platforms decides if your obby is fun.
cards.back: Use Move, Scale and Rotate to place each part. Start with easy jumps. If the start is too hard, players quit.
cards.tryit: Make your first 3 jumps easy, then make jump 4 a little harder.

cards.title: Anchor everything down
cards.front: Your platforms might fall the moment the game starts!
cards.back: Hold Shift, select all your new parts and turn on Anchor. Now they stay put, even when players bump them.
cards.tryit: Test once without anchoring and watch what happens. Then anchor everything.

cards.title: Test, then publish
cards.front: Real creators test their game again and again.
cards.back: Click Play with Test selected, try your course, then click Stop. Save with File, then Publish to Roblox.
cards.tryit: Ask Dad to sit with you and publish your obby together.

words.d: Short for obstacle course: a game where you jump past challenges.
A basic 3D shape in Roblox Studio, like a block or sphere.
A setting that locks a part in place so it can't fall.
Playing your own game to find what's broken or too hard.
Saving your game to Roblox so it's stored online.

quiz.q: Why should the first jumps in your obby be easy?
opts: Players may quit if the start is too hard
quiz.hint: Think about how you feel when a game is too hard right away.
quiz.why: Roblox's guide warns that a hard start makes players give up instead of continuing.

quiz.q: What happens to platforms that aren't anchored?
opts: They fall when the game starts
quiz.hint: Check card 4. What does Anchor stop?
quiz.why: Without Anchor, gravity pulls parts down as soon as the playtest begins.

quiz.q: Which tool changes how big a part is?
quiz.hint: Which word is about size, like a map's scale?
quiz.why: Scale makes parts bigger or smaller, while Move and Rotate change position and direction.

quiz.q: What's the best order for building an obby?
quiz.hint: You can't test something that isn't built yet.
quiz.why: Build first, lock parts down, test that it works, and then save it online.
